We present a two-stage neural approach for learning and refining correspondences between nodes in large, real-world graphs.

(1) we propose a new neural architecture for learning correspondences between graphs that is based on localized node embeddings and synchronous message passing networks; (2) we show that our architecture scales well to real-world inputs while consistently recovering global correspondences; (3) we demonstrate the practical effectiveness and state-of-the-art performance of our architecture on real-world tasks in computer vision and entity resolution between knowledge graphs

The main takeaway from our work is that
the consensus of local neighborhood correspondences is a well-founded measure for global structural correspondences, and can be used to guide the refinement process of soft correspondences.
deep learning methods for graph matching can be made scalable and effective, by leveraging local consensus in the matching process.
